title: Parameterize IBKRProvider's hardcoded 1h bar interval
description: get_hourly_bars hardcodes _BAR_INTERVAL = "1h" -- only hourly bars are implemented today, not the finer granularities (5-min/25-min/2-min, or 39-min/8-min) a future day-trader-mode feature would need. Parameterize the bar interval now so it's ready, without building the full day-trader-mode feature itself (that remains a separate, much larger idea explicitly flagged in docs/ideas.md as needing its own design pass -- not in scope here).

checklist.step: Generalize get_hourly_bars into a bar-interval-parameterized method (or add a `bar` parameter to it), validating the requested value against IBKR's actually-documented accepted bar values.
Default the parameter to today's '1h' behavior so no existing caller's behavior changes.
Record which bar values were confirmed vs. assumed (per this module's mocked-only testing constraint) as a decisions entry.
Update existing tests for the new parameter and add tests for at least one other interval value.

decisions.decision: Added a `bar_size: str = "1h"` keyword-only parameter to the existing `get_hourly_bars` method (kept its name unchanged) rather than renaming it to a generic `get_bars`/splitting into a new method, and validated it against a fixed `_VALID_BAR_INTERVALS` set: {1min, 2min, 3min, 5min, 10min, 15min, 30min, 1h, 2h, 3h, 4h, 8h, 1d, 1w, 1m} (raising ValueError before any network call for anything else).
decisions.rationale: The checklist explicitly offered both options ('generalize into a bar-interval-parameterized method (or add a `bar` parameter to it)'). No route or other module calls get_hourly_bars today (grepped app/ and tests/ outside test_ibkr_provider.py), so there was no back-compat risk from renaming, but keeping the name avoids rewriting the several docstring/architecture-doc cross-references that already call it 'get_hourly_bars' for no functional benefit, matching this task's own instruction not to scope-creep into the separate day-trader-mode design. The accepted bar-value set itself is IBKR's own publicly documented enumerated list for `GET /iserver/marketdata/history`'s `bar` query parameter (a fixed set of values, not a freely composable duration string) -- confirmed against IBKR's published Web API reference documentation, consistent with how every other value/shape in this module was implemented (this module's own docstring: 'implemented directly against IBKR's own documented Web API request/response shapes'). It is NOT verified against a live gateway response (no sandboxed/CI environment has one, per this module's existing testing constraint) -- that live-gateway verification remains deferred to manual testing by the user, same as every other endpoint this provider uses. One concrete, book-relevant consequence worth recording: docs/ideas.md's hypothetical '39-minute/8-minute' day-trader pairing (chosen because 39 divides the 390-minute trading day into 10 clean bars) is NOT achievable via this bar parameter at all -- IBKR's `bar` values are a fixed enumerated list, not arbitrary minute counts, so a future day-trader-mode design pass choosing that specific pairing would need a different mechanism (e.g. resampling 1-minute bars client-side) rather than requesting `bar=39min` directly.

decisions.decision: Changed the pagination cursor step (previously a hardcoded `timedelta(hours=1)` subtracted from the earliest bar's timestamp to compute the next page's `startTime`) to look up a per-`bar_size` step from a new `_BAR_INTERVAL_STEP` mapping.
decisions.rationale: The original hardcoded 1-hour step was correct only because the method only ever requested `bar=1h` bars; generalizing the `bar` parameter without also generalizing this step would silently skip up to ~59 minutes of bars between (earliest - one bar) and (earliest - 1h) whenever a finer interval (e.g. `5min`) was requested and multi-page pagination was needed -- a real correctness bug, not just a missed generalization, so fixing it was judged in-scope for 'parameterizing the existing hardcoded interval' rather than scope creep. `_MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES`'s 20-page safety bound was deliberately left unchanged (still sized against `1h` bars, ~833 days) -- a finer bar_size simply covers proportionally less history before hitting that same page cap, an acceptable, documented limitation rather than something worth redesigning here; a future day-trader-mode feature that genuinely needs deep finer-grained history would need to revisit that bound as part of its own larger design pass.
